conclusion: No sustained material RSS or active allocation regression was identified. All four original RSS increases failed to reproduce; default native buffer ownership and complete returned fields/sizes agree. Accept the selected integration without a memory implementation change.
interpretation: Observed system memory compression and allocator/residency variability are consistent with the unstable original RSS readings. This does not establish the exact OS cause or a memory speedup. Initial import-time reserved allocator space varies; it is distinct from in-use or resident memory and converges during the large native allocation stages.
limits: One host and limited directed repeats; this is a regression review, not a portable memory bound.
Native counters cover wind grids, operators and workspaces, not every allocation.
Darwin malloc-zone statistics exclude direct VM mappings; summed zone high-water values are not a simultaneous process peak.
The full-field hashing step touches returned pages; before/after phases are recorded separately.
The supported fixed-work flow results retain their existing physical and convergence limitations.
